records.name: North Korea
records.summary_text: North Korea is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely: same-sex conduct is not named in the Criminal Code, but Article 193 prohibits “decadent culture,” and broad obscene-activities provisions give the authorities unlimited discretion, and reported incidents of criminalisation and even execution for homosexuality exist. Gender identity does not exist in public life, visitors travel under constant escort and surveillance in the world's most totalitarian system, and any nonconforming presentation or discovered digital material risks detention, with no recorded protection or recognition

records.name: Palestinian Territories
records.summary_text:
Trans visitors face grave danger here, with a hard internal split: in the West Bank, same-sex conduct is not criminalised (Jordan's 1951 revision dropped consensual-private-sex offences, carried into the 1960 penal code applied there), but there are no protections, family/clan hostility is severe, and the Palestinian Authority has not legislated or signed key treaties. In the other part, Gaza, a 1936 British Mandate code technically allows up to 10 years for consensual same-sex acts, Hamas has executed people for alleged homosexuality, and the area is in a catastrophic war.

records.name: Sierra Leone
records.summary_text: Sierra Leone is dangerous for trans visitors. The 1861 Offences Against the Person Act criminalises buggery with up to life imprisonment (men only) — enforcement is limited but discrimination and violence are regular; no LGR; a small community organises quietly.
